title: Worked cases and exam-style problems
objectives: Identify the right formula for each question.
body_md:
Practise these patterns.

## 1. Futures P&L

Buy 3 lots (lot 75) at 480; close at 495. Profit = 15 × 75 × 3 = **₹3,375**.

## 2. Fair price

Spot 250, r 9%, 4 months: F = 250 × (1 + 0.09 × 4/12) = **257.5**.

## 3. Hedge

Portfolio ₹2 crore, β 0.9, futures 22,000, lot 50: N = 0.9 × 2,00,00,000 ÷ (22,000 × 50) ≈ **16.4**, so 16 lots.

## 4. Option payoff

Short put K = 300, premium 12, spot at expiry 280: loss = 20 − 12 = **8**.

## 5. Spread

Bear put spread: buy 200 put @9, sell 180 put @3: net debit 6, max gain 20 − 6 = **14**, max loss 6, breakeven 194.

## 6. Parity

S = 120, PV(K) = 115, P = 3: C = 3 + 5 = **8**.

## Tips

- Identify the **instrument**, **direction**, **units** (lot), then calculate.
- Check **signs**: buyer pays premium, seller receives.
- For breakevens, add or subtract the **total premium**.

> **Exam tip:** Write the formula first, then plug in; most errors come from lot size.
example: A short call K = 150, premium 4, spot at expiry 165: loss = 15 − 4 = 11 per unit.
say: Let me check the lot size and the sign before I calculate.
The breakeven is strike plus premium for a call buyer.
never: Ignore lot size, it is small.
Premium is paid by the seller.
